title: Searching, Pruning & Managing Image Bloat 🧹
description: Find images on registries, clean up old images, and keep your system lean.

slides.title: Finding Images: `docker search` 🔎
slides.content:
# Search Docker Hub from the CLI

```bash
docker search TERM
```

Finds public images on Docker Hub matching your term.

**Example:**
```bash
docker search python
```

Results include:
- **NAME**: image name
- **DESCRIPTION**: short description
- **STARS**: popularity
- **OFFICIAL**: `[OK]` if it’s an official image
- **AUTOMATED**: `[OK]` if auto‑built from a source repo (now deprecated)

> You can also search visually on [hub.docker.com](https://hub.docker.com) with better filters.

quizData.question: Does `docker search` search private registries by default?

options.text: Yes, it searches all registries configured
No, it searches only Docker Hub (and can be pointed to other registries with --limit or --filter)
It only searches the local image cache
It searches any public registry, but not private ones

quizData.explanation: `docker search` queries the Docker Hub by default. It does not search private registries unless you specify one with `--registry` (but this isn’t fully supported; better use the registry's own API/UI).

slides.title: Cleaning Up Unused Images 🧹
slides.content:
# `docker image prune`

Removes **dangling** images (those with `<none>` tag, often leftover from new builds).

```bash
docker image prune
```

Add `-a` to remove **all** images not currently referenced by any container:
```bash
docker image prune -a
```

Add `--filter` to target specific labels or timestamps:
```bash
docker image prune --filter "until=24h"
```

> Use with caution — `-a` will delete images you might want to keep.

slides.title: Disk Space Deep Dive 📉
slides.content:
# `docker system df`

Shows disk usage breakdown:

```bash
docker system df
```

Output:
- **Images**: total size, active, size reclaimable.
- **Containers**: similar.
- **Local Volumes**: size and reclaimable.
- **Build Cache**: size.

Add `-v` for verbose listing of each object.

To aggressively free up space:
```bash
docker system prune -a --volumes
```

This removes all stopped containers, unused networks, dangling images, build cache, and even unused volumes.

slides.title: System Cleanup Demo 🧹
slides.codeSnippet:
# See current usage
docker system df

# Remove dangling images
docker image prune

# Remove ALL unused images
docker image prune -a

# Aggressive cleanup (all stopped containers, unused networks, images, build cache)
docker system prune -a

# Also remove unused volumes
docker system prune -a --volumes

quizData.question: `docker image prune -a` will delete images that are currently used by stopped containers.
quizData.explanation: It only removes images not referenced by any container (running or stopped). If a stopped container still references an image, that image won’t be removed.

slides.title: Prune Danger ⚠️
slides.content:
## `-a` Deletes All Unused

If you run `docker image prune -a`, you might delete images you’ll need later. Always double‑check with `docker images` first. Consider using `--filter` to limit scope.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Automate Cleanup with Cron

On build servers, schedule `docker system prune -f --filter "until=72h"` to clean images older than 3 days. This prevents disk from filling up.
